title: Sacrifice and Offerings
lead: Gifts offered to God, from Cain and Abel's offerings (Genesis 4) and Noah's altar (Genesis 8:20) to the system of the Law (Leviticus 1–7), the prophets' warnings, and the New Testament's teaching that Christ's death is the final sacrifice (Hebrews 9–10).

sections.b: Before the Law, people bring gifts (minchah, Genesis 4:3–4) and whole burnt offerings (olah, Genesis 8:20; 22:2) and build altars at turning points (12:7; 26:25; 35:7). The Law at Sinai organizes burnt, grain, peace, sin and guilt offerings (Leviticus 1–7) and the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16). The prophets insist that God wants justice and loyalty more than offerings (1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6; Micah 6:6–8; Psalm 51:16–17). The New Testament presents Jesus as the Passover lamb (1 Corinthians 5:7) and a once-for-all sacrifice (Hebrews 9:11–14; 10:10–14), and calls believers to offer themselves (Romans 12:1).
